scope: Model support records are configuration-specific evidence links, not blanket compatibility guarantees. A product-level mapping is included only when the source explicitly identifies the accelerator product or generation. A documented recipe, an upstream verification matrix, a vendor report and an independently reproduced run are distinct evidence levels. Performance numbers belong in benchmark-results.json, not here. Newly added records in this revision distinguish exact checkpoint variants and keep vendor profile availability separate from upstream verification and independent testing.

support_levels.documented_recipe: Vendor or upstream documentation provides a runnable or step-by-step model deployment recipe for the named hardware configuration.
support_levels.upstream_verified: An upstream project explicitly lists or verifies the model on the named accelerator, but the record is not an independently reproduced benchmark by this project.
support_levels.vendor_reported: The vendor reports model support or testing; no upstream implementation or independent reproduction is implied.
support_levels.independently_tested: A reproducible third-party or project test with configuration and correctness evidence.
support_levels.integration_only: A framework integration exists but no exact model-level evidence has been located.

support_paths.quantization: BF16 checkpoint; no additional quantization asserted
support_paths.hardware_scope: AWS Trainium2 instance; tutorial uses tensor_parallel_size=64. This is an AWS deployment recipe, not a single-chip result.
support_paths.limitations: The recipe requires a Trn2 instance and matching Neuron SDK environment. Exact throughput, latency and model quality are not reported by this record.

evidence.claim: AWS provides a step-by-step Llama 3.1 405B deployment tutorial on Trainium2 using vLLM and NxD Inference; the sample uses BF16 and tensor parallel size 64.

support_paths.software_stack: vLLM Neuron plugin + Neuron SDK (Model Runner V1/V2)
support_paths.quantization: BF16 or static per-tensor FP8 ModelOpt checkpoint
support_paths.hardware_scope: AWS Trainium2 and Trainium3; the current AWS recipe explicitly lists both generations.
support_paths.limitations: Feature availability is model-runner and version dependent. AWS documents known data-parallel scaling limitations; this record does not imply all features are optimal or independently benchmarked.

evidence.claim: AWS documents Llama 3.3 70B Instruct on Trainium2 and Trainium3 with vLLM Neuron, BF16 and static FP8 ModelOpt, plus a model-specific feature matrix.

support_paths.software_stack: JetStream + MaxText + Pathways on Google Kubernetes Engine
support_paths.quantization: The tutorial describes BF16 and an INT8 MaxText-compatible checkpoint conversion path.
support_paths.hardware_scope: Google Cloud TPU v6e multi-host slice on GKE; the documented example uses TPU v6e topology 4x4.
support_paths.limitations: This is a specific JetStream/MaxText/Pathways deployment recipe. It does not establish model support on TPU7x or other TPU generations, nor vLLM/SGLang compatibility.

evidence.claim: Google's GKE tutorial serves Llama 3.1-405B on multi-host TPU v6e with JetStream, MaxText and Pathways; it documents BF16 and INT8 checkpoint paths.

support_paths.quantization: FP8 checkpoint; NVFP4 checkpoint for Blackwell; KV cache FP8 is configurable
support_paths.hardware_scope: NVIDIA Hopper and Blackwell. Curated recipes explicitly name H100/H200 and B200/GB200; detailed deployment guide documents backend/precision constraints for H100/H200, B200/GB200 and GB200 NVL72.
support_paths.limitations: Not every MoE backend supports every precision/device combination. For B200/GB200, the documented MoE backend depends on precision and EP size; do not generalize one recipe to all GPU counts or traffic shapes.

evidence.claim: TensorRT-LLM provides a DeepSeek-R1-0528 deployment guide with FP8 and NVFP4 checkpoints, curated H100/H200 and B200/GB200 configurations, and explicit MoE backend support constraints.

support_paths.software_stack: AMD Enterprise AI · Accelerator Inference Microservices (AIM)
support_paths.quantization: Not specified in the public accelerator support matrix; inspect the selected AIM profile before deployment.
support_paths.hardware_scope: AMD Instinct MI350X and MI355X are explicitly listed as optimized for DeepSeek-R1-0528 in the current AIM accelerator matrix.
support_paths.limitations: The matrix describes profile availability/support tier, not a universal framework-level guarantee or independent performance result. MI300X is listed for DeepSeek-R1 original in the matrix; this record is scoped to R1-0528 and MI350X/MI355X.

evidence.claim: AMD's current AIM accelerator matrix lists DeepSeek-R1-0528 as optimized on Instinct MI350X and MI355X; the support tier is based on available model-specific profiles.

support_paths.quantization: NVIDIA FP8 and NVFP4 checkpoints; NVFP4 is only supported on Blackwell.
support_paths.hardware_scope: NVIDIA Blackwell and Hopper architectures. Exact product SKU is not specified by the guide; NVFP4 is Blackwell-only.
support_paths.limitations: The source demonstrates a specific checkpoint and runtime version. Do not infer support for Llama 4 Maverick, other Scout variants, or every TensorRT-LLM release.

evidence.claim: NVIDIA documents Llama-4-Scout-17B-16E-Instruct FP8 serving on Hopper and Blackwell; NVFP4 is explicitly limited to Blackwell.

support_paths.quantization: Model checkpoint uses MXFP4 weights; the guide publishes B200 NVL configuration files.
support_paths.hardware_scope: NVIDIA B200 NVL configurations (4-GPU and 8-GPU configurations are listed). H200 configurations are also documented but are not mapped to a product record here.
support_paths.limitations: Recipe matrix is configuration-specific (GPU count, ISL/OSL, concurrency and TP size). This record intentionally does not map B200 NVL to B200 SXM or GB200 NVL72.

evidence.claim: NVIDIA publishes GPT-OSS-120B TensorRT-LLM serving configurations for 4xB200_NVL and 8xB200_NVL across multiple ISL/OSL and concurrency profiles.

support_paths.quantization: NVIDIA publishes BF16/base, FP8 and NVFP4 checkpoint variants; the recipe guide focuses on a working setup and recommended defaults.

support_paths.limitations: The guide lists Qwen3-235B-A22B, its FP8 checkpoint and NVFP4 checkpoint. It describes the setup as a functional quick start; additional optimizations/support are planned. It distinguishes the base model from Qwen3 Thinking variants.

evidence.claim: NVIDIA provides a Qwen3 TensorRT-LLM deployment guide and explicitly calls out MoE expert-parallel configuration for Qwen3-235B-A22B.
